title: Black beans, canned, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Black beans, canned with no added fat, are fully cooked beans preserved in their own juice or water. They retain most of their nutrients, are easy to digest, and convenient for quick meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) originated in Central and South America.
Canning without added fat keeps the calorie and fat content low.
The dark color comes from anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants.
They are a staple in Mexican and Latin American cuisines – in salsas, soups, and salads.
Properly stored cans can last 3–5 years.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A typical serving (about 130 g) provides roughly 8 g of protein, making it a valuable source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins help combat free radicals and support heart health.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned beans often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause digestive gas in sensitive people; introduce them gradually.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the beans to salads, soups, chili, tacos, rice dishes, or use them as a filling for burritos. They can also be mashed into a spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 4‑5 days.
